trickyParts: The host's one-shot timer cannot be cancelled (SessionContext.setTimeout returns void and there is no clearTimeout), so a single monotonic generation counter, bumped by every message_start, settle, phase-closed, delivered reminder and session change, is the whole defence against two armed timers sending two reminders. A reviewer should read phase-reminder.ts's armReminder with that in mind.

The continuation is bounded to one per run. The count resets on a tool call, and the reminder's own turn is one in which the worker is being told to call a tool, so gating the continuation on the count alone let a run continue itself without end, with no delay and no turn end for the daemon to see. The simplify pass found this; a separate run-scoped flag fixes it.

A reminder must not reset its own count. On Oh My Pi that is why it is pi.sendMessage with the legion-phase-reminder custom type and not sendUserMessage, which inboundKind would read as the daemon's assignment. On Claude Code the server keeps the exact text it last wrote to the inbox and compares the UserPromptSubmit prompt against it.
Claude Code ignores whatever a StopFailure hook returns, so that event can only record and arm a timer; it is also the one event of the five the pod measurements do not cover.

The npm wrapper package's bin/claude.exe is a stub its postinstall replaces. With --ignore-scripts the stub stays a stub, so the image links node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code-linux-x64/claude. Measured and recorded as a comment on the pull request.
